content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Identify the parts of a flower
Describe the functions of male and female flower parts
Explain how pollen and ovules are produced
Understand the role of flowers in sexual reproduction

(angiosperms) reproduce sexually using flowers. Flowers contain the reproductive organs that produce male gametes (in pollen) and female gametes (in ovules). Understanding flower structure is key to understanding plant reproduction.
Divides to form two male gametes
Tiny opening for pollen tube entry
Fuse with sperm to form endosperm
Male and female flowers on same plant
Male and female flowers on different plants
Pollen to stigma of same flower/plant
Pollen to stigma of different plant
Anthers and stigma mature at different times
Wind-pollinated flowers are often small and dull
Seeds develop from ovules in the ovary
Flowers are the reproductive organs of flowering plants
Stamens (male): anther produces pollen, filament supports
Carpel (female): stigma receives pollen, ovary contains ovules
Pollen contains male gametes; ovules contain female gametes
Wind-pollinated: small, no scent, lots of light pollen, feathery stigma
Many plants have mechanisms to prevent self-pollination
